strings.name: Kaiming He
strings.summary: Kaiming He studies computer vision and deep learning. Formerly at Microsoft Research Asia and Facebook AI Research, he is a tenured associate professor at MIT and a part-time distinguished scientist at Google DeepMind. With collaborators, he introduced methods including residual learning and Mask R-CNN, advancing deep-network training and image understanding. The papers and awards are collective achievements.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026, covering selected education, research, appointments and awards. Birth is confirmed only to the year; submission dates, effective appointments and awards are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Helped introduce residual networks and advance computer vision, influencing deep neural network training and image understanding.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth year
strings.facts.f1.value: 1984, according to a Tsinghua University alumni report.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BSc, Tsinghua University (2007); PhD, Chinese University of Hong Kong (2011).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Deep residual learning
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren and Jian Sun, introduced a residual-learning framework that improves training of deep neural networks.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Instance segmentation
strings.highlights.h2.text: With Georgia Gkioxari, Piotr Dollár and Ross Girshick, introduced Mask R-CNN to detect objects and predict a segmentation mask for each instance.
strings.timeline.t1.title: ResNet receives a test-of-time award
strings.timeline.t1.text: The co-authored paper receives the CVPR Longuet-Higgins Prize for its decade of influence on computer vision research.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Gains tenure at MIT
strings.timeline.t2.text: His tenured associate professorship takes effect, distinct from the appointment without tenure in 2024.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joins MIT faculty
strings.timeline.t3.text: Appointed associate professor without tenure in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Shares the Future Science Prize
strings.timeline.t4.text: Receives the Mathematics and Computer Science Prize with Jian Sun, Shaoqing Ren and Xiangyu Zhang for deep residual learning.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Submits the Mask R-CNN preprint
strings.timeline.t5.text: The four-author team releases its instance-segmentation preprint; this is the initial submission date.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Submits the ResNet preprint
strings.timeline.t6.text: The four-author team releases its deep residual learning paper, investigating optimization of deeper networks.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earns a doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Receives a PhD from the Chinese University of Hong Kong and joins Microsoft Research Asia that year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes undergraduate study
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earns a bachelor’s degree in the Basic Science Program of Tsinghua University’s physics department.
